source_text: Immersions and Zariski coverings of algebraic spaces

<STRUCT_0001>
At this point an interesting phenomenon occurs. We have already defined
the notion of an open immersion of algebraic spaces (through
Definition <REF_0001>)
but we have yet to define the notion of a <TEXTITOPEN_0001>point<TEXTITCLOSE_0001><FOOTNOTEOPEN_0001>We
will associate a topological space to an algebraic space in
Properties of Spaces, Section
<REF_0002>,
and its opens will correspond exactly to the open subspaces defined below.<FOOTNOTECLOSE_0001>.
Thus the <TEXTITOPEN_0002>Zariski topology<TEXTITCLOSE_0002> of an algebraic space
has already been defined, but there is no space yet!

<STRUCT_0002><STRUCT_0003>
Perhaps superfluously we formally introduce immersions as follows.

Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme.
Let <MATH_0002> be an algebraic space over <MATH_0003>.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> A morphism of algebraic spaces over <MATH_0004>
is called an <TEXTITOPEN_0001>open immersion<TEXTITCLOSE_0001> if it is representable, and an open immersion
in the sense of Definition <REF_0001>.
<STRUCT_0003> An <TEXTITOPEN_0002>open subspace<TEXTITCLOSE_0002> of <MATH_0005> is a subfunctor <MATH_0006>
such that <MATH_0007> is an algebraic space and <MATH_0008> is an
open immersion.
<STRUCT_0004> A morphism of algebraic spaces over <MATH_0009>
is called a <TEXTITOPEN_0003>closed immersion<TEXTITCLOSE_0003> if it is representable, and a closed
immersion in the sense of
Definition <REF_0002>.
<STRUCT_0005> A <TEXTITOPEN_0004>closed subspace<TEXTITCLOSE_0004> of <MATH_0010> is a subfunctor <MATH_0011>
such that <MATH_0012> is an algebraic space and <MATH_0013> is a
closed immersion.
<STRUCT_0006> A morphism of algebraic spaces over <MATH_0014>
is called an <TEXTITOPEN_0005>immersion<TEXTITCLOSE_0005> if it is representable, and an immersion
in the sense of Definition <REF_0003>.
<STRUCT_0007> A <TEXTITOPEN_0006>locally closed subspace<TEXTITCLOSE_0006> of <MATH_0015> is a subfunctor <MATH_0016>
such that <MATH_0017> is an algebraic space and <MATH_0018> is an
immersion.
<STRUCT_0008>
